# Introduction

Overview
The ggplot2 package (part of the Tidyverse) provides a powerful system for creating graphics in R by implementing the Grammar of Graphics. It uses layers to gradually build complex visualizations from simple components.
Packages and Key Functions:

- `ggplot2` (key functions include `ggplot()`, `aes()`, `geom_point()`, `geom_bar()`, `geom_line()`, `geom_histogram()`, `facet_wrap()`, `theme()`, etc.)

Use Cases

- Exploratory data analysis: Quick visualization of relationships in data.
- Publication-ready plots: Highly customizable appearance and layout.
- Interactive or iterative workflows: Build complex visuals step-by-step.

Benefits

- Layered approach allows modular building of plots.
- Consistent grammar for different plot types.
- Powerful customizations (labels, scales, themes, etc.).

```r
ggplot2::ggplot(data, aes(x, y)) + geom_*()
```

(The skeleton structure above demonstrates how layers are added; it is not meant to run by itself.)

Below is a schematic (using Mermaid) illustrating the layered approach in ggplot2:

```{mermaid}
graph LR
    A["Begin with ggplot()"] --> B["Add aes() layer"]
    B --> C["Add geom_*() layer"]
    C --> D["Optional: Add facet or theme layers"]
```

# Getting Started

Loading the Package
You can load ggplot2 with pacman::p_load():


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
pacman::p_load(ggplot2)
```
:::


Basic Usage
Below is a simple example to illustrate the core functionality of ggplot2. We will use the built-in mtcars dataset to create a scatter plot of `mpg` (miles per gallon) vs. `hp` (horsepower).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Scatter plot of mpg vs. hp
mtcars |>
    ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = hp, y = mpg)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Basic Scatter Plot",
        x = "Horsepower",
        y = "Miles Per Gallon"
    )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


In this code:

- mtcars is piped into ggplot2::ggplot().
- ggplot2::aes() maps hp to the x-axis and mpg to the y-axis.
- ggplot2::geom_point() adds the point geometry to create a scatter plot.
- ggplot2::labs() customizes labels.

# Key Functions and Features

ggplot2::ggplot()
Description

- The main function to initialize a ggplot object, where you specify the dataset and general aesthetic mappings.

Syntax

```r
ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(...))
```

- data: A data frame.
- ggplot2::aes(…): Aesthetic mappings for x, y, color, size, etc.

Example


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Basic template (with mpg dataset from ggplot2)
ggplot2::ggplot(data = ggplot2::mpg, ggplot2::aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


ggplot2::aes()
Description

- Defines the mapping of variables to visual properties (aesthetics) such as x, y, color, fill, size, shape, and more.

Syntax

```r
ggplot2::aes(x, y, color = ..., fill = ..., shape = ...)
```

Example


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::mpg, ggplot2::aes(x = cyl, y = hwy, color = drv)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


- Here, drv is mapped to color, creating different point colors by drive type.

ggplot2::geom_*()
Description

- A family of geometric functions to specify how data points are represented (points, lines, bars, etc.).

Syntax

```r
ggplot2::geom_point(...)
ggplot2::geom_line(...)
ggplot2::geom_bar(...)
ggplot2::geom_histogram(...)
```

Arguments often include statistical transformations, bin widths, position adjustments, etc.

Example: Bar Plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::mpg, ggplot2::aes(x = class)) +
    ggplot2::geom_bar()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


- Displays the count of each vehicle class in the mpg dataset.

ggplot2::facet_wrap()
Description

- Splits data into subplots (facets) based on one or more categorical variables.

Syntax

```r
ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ variable, ncol = ...)
```

Example


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::mpg, ggplot2::aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~drv)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


- Creates separate panels for each drive type (drv).

ggplot2::theme()
Description

- Adjusts non-data components (text size, legend placement, background, etc.).

Syntax

```r
ggplot2::theme(
  panel.background = element_rect(...),
  axis.text.x = element_text(...),
  ...
)
```

Example


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::mpg, ggplot2::aes(x = displ, y = hwy)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


- Applies a minimal theme to reduce chart ink and highlight data.

# In-Depth Examples

Title: Comparing Engine Displacement and Fuel Efficiency
Objective

- Visualize relationships between engine displacement (displ) and highway fuel efficiency (hwy) for different car classes.

Steps

1. Data Preparation
   We will use the built-in mpg dataset and select relevant columns: displ, hwy, class.

2. Function Application
   - Initialize the plot with ggplot2::ggplot().
   - Map displ and hwy using ggplot2::aes().
   - Add geom_point().
   - Facet the plot by car class using ggplot2::facet_wrap().
   - Add a custom theme.

3. Visualization


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Step-by-step example
filtered_mpg <- ggplot2::mpg

filtered_mpg |>
    ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = class)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~class) +
    ggplot2::theme_bw() +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Engine Displacement vs. Highway MPG by Class",
        subtitle = "Faceted by Vehicle Class",
        x = "Engine Displacement (Liters)",
        y = "Highway Miles per Gallon",
        color = "Vehicle Class"
    )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


Output

- You will see a facetted scatter plot showing how different classes compare in the displ-hwy relationship. The color indicates each class, and each facet displays data for one class.

# Advanced Features

Customization

- Modify legends, labels, and scales with functions like ggplot2::labs(), ggplot2::scale_color_manual(), or ggplot2::theme().
- Adjust axis transformations (e.g., log scale) with ggplot2::scale_x_log10() or ggplot2::scale_y_log10().

Integration

- Combine ggplot2 with dplyr for data wrangling:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)

ggplot2::mpg |>
    dplyr::filter(displ < 5) |>
    ggplot2::ggplot(ggplot2::aes(x = displ, y = cty)) +
    ggplot2::geom_point() +
    ggplot2::geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](ggplot2_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


- This uses dplyr::filter() to remove rows with displacement >= 5, then plots with ggplot2.

Optimization

- For large datasets, consider sampling or binning (geom_bin2d, geom_hex from other packages).
- Use efficient data handling (data.table or arrow) before feeding data to ggplot2 for plotting.
- Limit layering of overly detailed geoms when performance is a concern.

# Troubleshooting and FAQs

Common Issues

- "Error in ggplot(…): object not found": Ensure the dataset or column name matches correctly and is in scope.
- "Discrete value supplied to continuous scale": A variable mapped to x or y might be character instead of numeric; convert if necessary.
- Missing + sign between layers: Each layer is added with the + operator; forgetting it can break the chain of commands.

FAQs

1. How do I rotate x-axis labels?
   - Use ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1)).
2. Can I save my plots?
   - Yes, with ggplot2::ggsave("plot.png", width = …, height = …).
3. How do I create interactive plots?
   - Use packages like plotly or ggiraph that build on ggplot2.

# Best Practices

- Keep code modular: Prepare and clean data first, then pipe into ggplot2 functions.
- Use meaningful variable and aesthetic mappings for readability.
- Write reproducible scripts by incorporating set.seed() for sampling or random processes.
- When presenting results (including power analysis in broader data workflows), ensure the data, code, and figure output are clearly documented.

# Conclusion

Summary
We have explored the ggplot2 package's layered approach to building plots, introduced key functions, and provided examples for customizing, faceting, and integrating with other data pipelines.

Next Steps

- Experiment with specialized geoms (e.g., boxplots, violin plots).
- Explore advanced theming options (e.g., ggthemes package).
- Investigate extension packages like gganimate for animated graphics or patchwork for arranging multiple ggplots.
